---
title: "Analytical chemistry glossary"
---

## Measurand

The quantity intended to be measured, including the analyte, material and concentration or amount basis.

## Sample

Material selected from a defined population or lot. Repeated readings of one preparation are not additional collected samples.

## Aliquot

A measured portion taken from a sample or solution.

## Dilution factor

Final total volume divided by aliquot volume, when dilution conserves analyte and volumes share units.

## Calibration

An established relationship between a measured response and known input quantities under specified conditions.

## Residual

Observed response minus the response predicted by the fitted model.

## Precision

Agreement among repeated measurements under specified conditions; it does not establish freedom from bias.

## Bias

An estimate of systematic departure from a reference quantity.

## Standard uncertainty

An uncertainty expressed as a standard deviation within a stated measurement model.

## Recovery

A measured quantity relative to a known added or reference quantity, with the preparation and concentration basis stated.

## Matrix effect

A change in analyte response caused by other sample components.

## Quality control

Checks, including method blanks and independent reference materials, used to assess whether the measurement process meets stated criteria. A passing check does not establish every aspect of method validity.

## Activity

A dimensionless effective concentration, for example $a=\gamma c/c^\circ$ in a specified concentration convention. An electrode responds to activity under the stated model; matching conditions may permit calibration in concentration.

## Equivalence point

The titrant amount satisfying the chosen reaction stoichiometry.

## Endpoint

The observed experimental criterion used to locate completion; it can differ from equivalence.

## Absorbance

The negative base-ten logarithm of transmittance, A = −log₁₀(I/I₀).

## Retention time

Elapsed time between injection and the defined peak location in a chromatogram.

## Resolution

A measure of separation relative to peak widths; state the width convention when calculating it.

## Internal standard

A deliberately added reference compound used to normalize response. It corrects only effects that it shares appropriately with the analyte.

## Selectivity

The extent to which the procedure measures the intended analyte in the presence of other components.
